newsitem.title: MEXICO: Rebel killed, 2 soldiers wounded in Mexico attack.
newsitem.headline: Rebel killed, 2 soldiers wounded in Mexico attack.

text.p: A presumed member of the rebel Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) was killed early on Monday and two soldiers were wounded during a clash in the southern Mexican state of Guerrero, officials said.

The Mexican army said two of its men were injured when gunmen opened fire on them before dawn. "While repelling the attack, an individual armed with an AK-47 rifle was killed," it said in a statement.
The army did not identify the gunmen, but a judicial official told Reuters the dead man was wearing a uniform that showed him to be a member of the EPR.
He was found by the side of the road near Aguas Blancas, some 20 miles (32 kms) northwest of Acapulco, at the site where the EPR first announced its existence at a left-wing rally on June 28.
"By his appearence, he was from the EPR," said Ramon Almonte, a prosecutor in the tourist resort of Acapulco who was heading an investigation into the killing.

Almonte said the dead man, who he identified as Benjamin Avila Blanco, 21, was found wearing the olive green and coffee-coloured uniform of the EPR. His face was masked and he wore a cap similar to those seen in EPR videos, he added.

Television network TV Azteca reported that five masked gunmen clashed with a 150-strong army unit early on Saturday near Aguas Blancas. It said three rucksacks containing explosives were found among the dead man's possessions.
Radio Red quoted a local mayor as saying some 60 EPR members held a vigil overnight at the site in Aguas Blancas where 17 peasants were gunned down by police in June 1995.

The EPR's main assaults to date have been against police and soldiers. Some 15 people were killed and 22 wounded in a coordinated series of strikes on August 28-29 in several Mexican states, according to official figures.
Mexican authorities were on a state of alert for rebel attacks during Independence Day celebrations on Sunday and Monday, but most of the country was calm, officials said.

On Friday, in a rare news conference in the state of Oaxaca, bordering Guerrero, an EPR commander threatened to step up attacks on government troops if the rebels considered that military repression of local inhabitants was on the rise.
